The eruption is characterized by a circular shock front seen in EUV imagery, particularly in GOES SUVI 284 imagery as there was an ongoing SDO AIA outage at the time.

data.note: Faint CME first seen to the SE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-07-07T15:12Z. This CME fades before exiting the field of view in SOHO LASCO C2 and is therefore not visible in other coronagraphs. The source of this event is an M4.0 flare from Active Region 14482 (S11E50) peaking at 2026-07-07T14:19Z as seen in SDO AIA 131. Dimming and field line movement is also visible in SDO AIA 171/193, along with some filament material seen in SDO AIA 304, although most of this material appears to get reabsorbed and falls back to the solar surface.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2.

data.note: CME first seen to the NE beginning at 2026-07-07T22:12Z by SOHO LASCO C2, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source of this event is a large filament eruption seen centered at approx. N20E70 with liftoff beginning at approx. 2026-07-07T21:33Z as seen in SDO AIA and GOES SUVI 304. Field line opening, dimming and post eruptive arcades are also seen in SDO AIA 171, 193 and GOES SUVI 284.

N17W121) as seen in STEREO A EUVI imagery, with moving field lines and brightening seen from the regions around 2026-07-08T06:00Z-07:00Z, but it is difficult to tell from the perspective of STEREO A EUVI imagery.

The source is likely an eruption with opening field lines starting around 2026-07-08T08:25Z in STEREO A EUV 195 imagery. The exact source location on the disk as seen from STEREO A is unclear, as the source is near the west limb.

data.note: Possibly two overlapping CMEs visible to the E in STEREO A COR2 imagery and to the S/SW in GOES CCOR-1 imagery starting at 2026-07-09T07:53Z and 2026-07-09T08:23Z based on STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source of this CME(s) is an eruption from the area of Active Region 14485 (S10W34) starting around 2026-07-09T06:56Z to the SW in GOES SUVI 195 with additional eruption signatures to the NW of AR 14485 (S10W34) in GOES SUVI 195 starting around 2026-07-09T07:08Z. There is a following eruption starting around 2026-07-09T07:48Z with associated brightening and dimming to the N/NW of the Active Region spanning roughly from W25 to W10 and S00 to S12. An EUV wave is visible in GOES SUVI 284 following the main eruption with post-eruptive arcades starting around 2026-07-09T08:53Z as seen in GOES SUVI 195 and 284. These eruptions are also visible in STEREO A EUV 195 and 304 as well as in SDO/AIA wavelengths following an eclipse.

The source may be related to an eruption from Active Region 14484 (N15W50) starting around 2026-07-09T20:45Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/193/304 and GOES SUVI 131/195/284/304 imagery. A subsequent opening of field lines is visible over the northwest limb at this time in SDO AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 284 imagery as well.

data.note: CME observed to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source is far-sided from Earth, observed as field line movement beyond the West limb in GOES SUVI 171/195/284 starting roughly around 2026-07-10T09:21Z. May also be observed in STEREO A EUVI 195 on its west limb over former AR 14479, with loops over this region brightening starting around 2026-07-10T08:35Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source is a minor eruption centered around S20E60, observed as dimming and field line movement in GOES SUVI 195 starting around 2026-07-10T07:28Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2.

The source is a filament eruption near the east limb centered ~N06E63 beginning as early as 2026-07-10T12:18Z in SDO AIA 304 with the filament brightening and agitating, and more eruptively lifting off around 2026-07-10T13:33Z although the majority of the material seems to reabsorb onto the disk. Also observed as field line movement in SDO AIA 171/193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: CME observed to the SW in STEREO A COR2, GOES CCOR-1, and SOHO LASCO C2/C3 after a downlink gap backfilled in. The source is AR 14485 and a C6.0 flare (S16W47) peaking at 2026-07-10T14:59Z. Also observed well in SDO AIA 171/193 as field line movement, pockets of dimming in the vicinity (not a central area), and a minor EUV wave.

Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 of a faint shock feature best observed in LASCO C2's field-of-view, noting it does measure slower than the bulk.

data.note: CME observed to the NW only in SOHO LASCO C2, likely due to diffusing and becoming too faint ot resolve after earliest frames. The source is likely a weak filament ejecta and field line movement centered ~N15W65 in SDO AIA 171/193 starting around 2026-07-10T23:15Z, in proximity to a nearby coronal hole.

cmeAnalyses.note: 3D SOHO LASCO C2 only analysis using the observed source around W65 as an estimate, as such parameters could slightly vary.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the NE in STEREO A COR2, and NNW in SOHO LASCO C2, also NNW but heavily pylon obscured in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The source is likely a large, diffuse area of slow dimming and field line movement on the NW disk in SDO AIA 171/193, starting as early as 2026-07-11T20:30Z and centered approximately around N45W35. This diffuse, slow source is likely also responsible for the following, overlapping CME: 2026-07-11T04:38Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2, as the CME is blocked by the pylon in LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and also too faint to resolve in running difference imagery beyond earliest frames.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the NE in STEREO A COR2, and NNW in SOHO LASCO C2, also NNW but heavily pylon obscured in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The source is likely a large, diffuse area of slow dimming and field line movement on the NW disk in SDO AIA 171/193, starting as early as 2026-07-11T20:30Z and centered approximately around N45W35, and may be separable with more weak field line movement to the NW in SDO AIA 171 around 2026-07-11T02:51Z but it is not too distinct. This diffuse, slow source is likely also responsible for the preceeding, overlapping CME: 2026-07-11T01:23Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2, as the CME is partially blocked by the pylon in LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1.

data.note: CME observed to the W in STEREO A COR2 and W/SW GOES CCOR-1, not in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in real-time due to an ongoing outage. The source of the CME is likely former Active Region 14479 or AR 14478, estimated to be located ~N17W165 and ~S05W155 at this time. There are two potential eruptive signatures observed on/around the west limb in STEREO A EUVI: one as wide field line breaking and EUV wave in EUVI 195 to the SW starting around 2026-07-11T15:05Z, and prominence movement and brightening in EUVI 304 to the NW starting around 2026-07-11T15:45Z. Of these, the SW field line movement appears to be a better fit based on timing and CME LE/SH appearance.

Shock front triangulation between STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

data.note: CME observed to the W in STEREO A COR2 and W/SW GOES CCOR-1 following behind the 2026-07-11T16:09Z CME, not in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in real-time due to an ongoing outage. The source of the CME may likely involve former Active Region 14479 or AR 14478, estimated to be located ~N17W165 and ~S05W155 at this time.

data.note: CME seen to the Southwest in SOHO LASCO C2 in association with a long-duration C5.9-class flare from AR 14485 (S10W68) with corresponding circular EUV wave seen best in GOES SUVI 284 imagery starting around 2026-07-12T01:00Z. This eruption is located to the South of a prominent coronal hole, resulting in this CME likely being deflected. This CME overlaps with CME: 2026-0712T02:12Z. This subsequent CME (CME: 2026-07-12T02:12Z) appears to accelerate the Northern portion of this ongoing event (CME: 2026-07-12T02:14Z), greatly changing its morphology in later frames.

data.note: CME first seen to the NW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-07-12T02:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The CME is seen to the NE in STEREO A COR2. The source of this event is a region of dimming seen located at approximately N10W45 beginning at approximately 2026-07-12T01:45Z as seen in SDO AIA 193. However, due to coronal hole proximity, this CME is likely deflected from the source location. This dimming is likely residual/expanded dimming following a C5.3 flare from Active Region 14485. This CME heavily overlaps and disturbs the morphology of CME: 2026-07-12T01:14Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2.

The source of this CME is a small eruption seen beyond the West limb by STEREO A EUVI 304 beginning at approx. 2026-07-12T03:45Z.

The source of this event is an M1.1 flare from Active Region 14485 (S10W68) which peaked at 2026-07-12T08:11Z as seen in SDO AIA 131. Field line opening and post eruptive arcades are also seen in association with this flare in SDO AIA 171 and 193. This CME is likely deflected due to the eruption proximity to a prominent coronal hole.

data.note: CME first seen to the SE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-07-13T19:36Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap beginning at 2026-07-13T18:53Z. The source of this event is likely far sided as no clear eruptions are visible on the disk, but field line movement is visible from beyond the SE limb in GOES SUVI 284 beginning at approx. 2026-07-13T19:00Z. An estimated C9 flare is seen from preliminary Solar Orbiter STIX data, possibly from Active Region 14478, which rotated off of the Earth-facing disk around 2026-07-07. The approximate source longitude estimated from preliminary Solar Orbiter magnetogram data is S05W180.

The source is an eruption visible from beyond the western limb likely from former Active Region 14485 (~S10W110) starting around 2026-07-15T02:30Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery. Additionally, dimming is observed from the eruption site starting around 2026-07-15T02:55Z seen in STEREO A EUVI 195 imagery.
